page.layout: One page of running text in one column. Running head at top, printed page number 135 at top right. Catchword at the foot right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: Sint preces meæ & patientia velut aqua offusa quâ mitescant vel extinguantur linguæ Igneæ, quæ à Gehenna jam diu accendi videntur, & inter malitiosas illas flammas æstuare.

p.i: Des eorum maledicta benefaciendo[?] vel refellere omnino, vel silentium imponere. Ne gaudeant fructu labiorum suorum, sed Orationis meæ potius pœnitentiam illis & veniam precantis.

main_text.p: Instrue me Davidis patientiâ & pietate Hezekiæ, ut per eorum virulentiam misericordiam tuam perspiciam & in eorum peccato Iustitiam.
Ille Turbidæ Shebæ conciones, illa Rab-shekah opprobria, & execratio Shimei, preces meas humiles lacessant, & repetitas Tuas in Me benedictiones.

p.i: Licet illi maledicant, tu benedicas, & bene-dictus ero[?], & benedictio fiam populo meo.
Et Lapis quem reprobaverunt ædificantes, factus erit in Caput Anguli.
Prospice me de excelso Sancto tuo, & libera me ab iis qui me absorbere cupiunt.
Absconde me in conspectu tuo à superbia hominum malorum, & à contradictione linguarum serva me.

page.notes: The page ends with a small ornament after "serva me." which is not text and is not transcribed. Two readings are doubtful: "benefaciendo" (the middle letters look like "ci" or "ie") and "ero" at the end of "bene-dictus" (the scan reads more like "cro"). The italic and roman distinctions in the Shebæ/Shimei and Davidis/Hezekiæ lines are approximate, since those words are set in larger type.
